Edited Oct 20, 2025: I used Gemini to write a minimal, self-contained PyTorch script for the reproduction of the issue. It does not require the YOLOv8 project that I originally encountered the issue in.

### Problem Description

A `not a valid operand` error for `MIOpenBatchNormFwdTrainSpatial` occurs in torch.nn.BatchNorm2d when running a forward pass in training mode. 

This issue is consistently reproducible on both Ubuntu and Windows, using recent ROCm and PyTorch nightly builds.

### Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS (Noble Numbat), Windows 10 Pro 21H2 10.0.19044

### CPU

AMD RYZEN AI MAX+ 395 w/ Radeon 8060S

### GPU

AMD Radeon(TM) 8060S Graphics

### ROCm Version

Linux: 7.0.2, Windows: 7.10.0a20251016

### ROCm Component

MIOpen

### Steps to Reproduce

On Ubuntu Linux:
1. Installation of ROCm: I followed the guide on [/rocm.docs.amd.com](https://rocm.docs.amd.com/projects/install-on-linux/en/latest/install/quick-start.html) and ran the following comands for ROCm and AMDGPU driver installation
```
wget https://repo.radeon.com/amdgpu-install/7.0.2/ubuntu/noble/amdgpu-install_7.0.2.70002-1_all.deb
sudo apt install ./amdgpu-install_7.0.2.70002-1_all.deb
sudo apt update
sudo apt install python3-setuptools python3-wheel
sudo usermod -a -G render,video $LOGNAME # Add the current user to the render and video groups
sudo apt install rocm
```
```
wget https://repo.radeon.com/amdgpu-install/7.0.2/ubuntu/noble/amdgpu-install_7.0.2.70002-1_all.deb
sudo apt install ./amdgpu-install_7.0.2.70002-1_all.deb
sudo apt update
sudo apt install "linux-headers-$(uname -r)" "linux-modules-extra-$(uname -r)"
sudo apt install amdgpu-dkms
```
2. Setting up the Python environment:
I installed miniconda3, created a virtual environment and installed the preview ROCm version of Pytorch on [pytorch.org](https://pytorch.org/) with
```pip3 install --pre torch torchvision --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/nightly/rocm7.0```
I then installed necessary libraries, mainly `ultralytics` and `transformers` to run YOLO. 

On Windows 10:
1. Installation of the AMD graphics driver:
I obtained and installed AMD Graphics Driver version 32.0.12045 from my laptop manufacturer's [website](https://rog.asus.com/laptops/rog-flow/rog-flow-z13-2025/helpdesk_download/).

2. Setting up the Python environment:
I installed miniconda3, created a virtual environment and installed the preview, prebuilt ROCm wheels for Windows from [theRock](https://github.com/ROCm/TheRock/tree/main). I manually checked the build status, picked the most recent one with all torch wheels built successfully, and installed with the command
```
python -m pip install --index-url https://rocm.nightlies.amd.com/v2/gfx1151/ rocm==7.10.0a20251016
```
```
C:/ProgramData/miniconda3/envs/torch-rocm-20251018-py312/python.exe -m pip install --pre --index-url https://rocm.nightlies.amd.com/v2/gfx1151/torch/ --extra-index-url https://rocm.nightlies.amd.com/v2/gfx1151/torchaudio/ --extra-index-url https://rocm.nightlies.amd.com/v2/gfx1151/torchvision/ --extra-index-url https://rocm.nightlies.amd.com/v2/gfx1151/ ./torch-2.10.0a0+rocm7.10.0a20251016-cp312-cp312-win_amd64.whl ./torchaudio-2.8.0a0+rocm7.10.0a20251016-cp312-cp312-win_amd64.whl ./torchvision-0.25.0a0+rocm7.10.0a20251016-cp312-cp312-win_amd64.whl
```

**For both Linux and Windows:**
3. Either of the minimal reproduction script below will produce the error.

<details>
<summary>Python script with AMP disabled</summary>
<pre># This script is the direct output of Google's Gemini LLM model.<br># I ran the script to verify that it reproduced the same MIOpen error<br># as the ultralytics YOLOv8 model that I was working with.<br>import torch<br>import torch.nn as nn<br><br># --------------------------------------------------------------------------<br># Configuration<br># --------------------------------------------------------------------------<br>BATCH_SIZE = 100<br>IMG_HEIGHT = 640<br>IMG_WIDTH = 640<br>IN_CHANNELS = 3<br>OUT_CHANNELS = 32<br>KERNEL_SIZE = 3<br>STRIDE = 2<br>DEVICE = 'cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu'<br><br># --------------------------------------------------------------------------<br># Minimal Model<br># --------------------------------------------------------------------------<br>class MinimalReproducer(nn.Module):<br>    def __init__(self):<br>        super().__init__()<br>        self.conv_block = nn.Sequential(<br>            nn.Conv2d(<br>                in_channels=IN_CHANNELS,<br>                out_channels=OUT_CHANNELS,<br>                kernel_size=KERNEL_SIZE,<br>                stride=STRIDE,<br>                padding=1,<br>                bias=False<br>            ),<br>            nn.BatchNorm2d(OUT_CHANNELS)<br>        )<br><br>    def forward(self, x):<br>        return self.conv_block(x)<br><br># --------------------------------------------------------------------------<br># Main script execution<br># --------------------------------------------------------------------------<br>if __name__ == "__main__":<br>    if DEVICE == 'cpu':<br>        print("CUDA (ROCm) device not found.")<br>        exit()<br><br>    print(f"Running on device: {torch.cuda.get_device_name(0)}")<br>    print("Testing with Automatic Mixed Precision (AMP) DISABLED.\n")<br><br>    # 1. Instantiate the model<br>    model = MinimalReproducer().to(DEVICE)<br>    model.train()<br><br>    # 2. Create a dummy input tensor with full precision (float32)<br>    dummy_input = torch.randn(BATCH_SIZE, IN_CHANNELS, IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH, device=DEVICE, dtype=torch.float32)<br>    print(f"Created a dummy input tensor of shape: {dummy_input.shape} and dtype: {dummy_input.dtype}")<br><br>    try:<br>        # 3. Perform the forward pass without the amp.autocast() context manager<br>        print("\nExecuting forward pass in full precision (float32)...")<br>        output = model(dummy_input)<br>        print("Forward pass completed successfully without error.")<br>        print(f"Output tensor shape: {output.shape}")<br><br>    except RuntimeError as e:<br>        # This block will catch the error if it still occurs even without AMP<br>        print(f"\nAn error occurred even with AMP disabled!")<br>        print("---------------------------------------")<br>        print(f"Caught RuntimeError: {e}")<br>        print("---------------------------------------")</pre>
</details>


<details>
<summary>Python script with AMP enabled:</summary>
<pre># This script is the direct output of Google's Gemini LLM model.<br># I ran the script to verify that it reproduced the same MIOpen error<br># as the ultralytics YOLOv8 model that I was working with.<br>import torch<br>import torch.nn as nn<br><br># --------------------------------------------------------------------------<br># Configuration to match the YOLOv8 training environment that causes the bug<br># --------------------------------------------------------------------------<br># From YOLO log: batch=100, imgsz=640, input channels=3 (standard for images)<br>BATCH_SIZE = 100<br>IMG_HEIGHT = 640<br>IMG_WIDTH = 640<br>IN_CHANNELS = 3<br><br># From YOLO model summary: The first layer is a Conv with 32 output channels.<br>#   0  -1  1  928  ultralytics.nn.modules.conv.Conv [3, 32, 3, 2]<br>OUT_CHANNELS = 32<br>KERNEL_SIZE = 3<br>STRIDE = 2<br><br># The device should be the ROCm-enabled GPU, which PyTorch refers to as 'cuda'<br>DEVICE = 'cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu'<br><br># --------------------------------------------------------------------------<br># Minimal Model to replicate the failing operation<br># The YOLO traceback points to an error in batch normalization (self.bn)<br># which is called right after a convolution (self.conv).<br># --------------------------------------------------------------------------<br>class MinimalReproducer(nn.Module):<br>    def __init__(self):<br>        super().__init__()<br>        # This single block mimics the first layer of yolov8s where the error occurs<br>        self.conv_block = nn.Sequential(<br>            nn.Conv2d(<br>                in_channels=IN_CHANNELS,<br>                out_channels=OUT_CHANNELS,<br>                kernel_size=KERNEL_SIZE,<br>                stride=STRIDE,<br>                padding=1, # Standard padding for a 3x3 kernel<br>                bias=False  # BatchNorm makes conv bias redundant<br>            ),<br>            nn.BatchNorm2d(OUT_CHANNELS)<br>        )<br><br>    def forward(self, x):<br>        return self.conv_block(x)<br><br># --------------------------------------------------------------------------<br># Main script execution<br># --------------------------------------------------------------------------<br>if __name__ == "__main__":<br>    if DEVICE == 'cpu':<br>        print("CUDA (ROCm) device not found. This script will not be able to reproduce the GPU-specific MIOpen bug.")<br>        exit()<br><br>    print(f"Running on device: {torch.cuda.get_device_name(0)}")<br>    print("Attempting to reproduce the MIOpen BatchNorm compilation error...\n")<br><br>    # 1. Instantiate the minimal model<br>    model = MinimalReproducer().to(DEVICE)<br>    # Set the model to training mode, as the error is in `MIOpenBatchNormFwdTrainSpatialHIP.cpp`<br>    model.train()<br><br>    # 2. Create a dummy input tensor with the same dimensions as the YOLO model's input<br>    # Shape: (batch_size, channels, height, width)<br>    dummy_input = torch.randn(BATCH_SIZE, IN_CHANNELS, IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH, device=DEVICE, dtype=torch.float16)<br>    print(f"Created a dummy input tensor of shape: {dummy_input.shape} and dtype: {dummy_input.dtype}")<br><br>    try:<br>        # 3. Use Automatic Mixed Precision (AMP), as YOLO log shows `amp=True`.<br>        # This is crucial for reproducing the bug.<br>        with torch.cuda.amp.autocast():<br>            # 4. Perform the forward pass. This is the step that should trigger the MIOpen error.<br>            print("\nExecuting forward pass... This is expected to fail with a 'miopenStatusUnknownError'.")<br>            output = model(dummy_input)<br>            print("Forward pass completed without error (bug not reproduced).")<br>            print(f"Output tensor shape: {output.shape}")<br><br>    except RuntimeError as e:<br>        print(f"\nSuccessfully reproduced the error!")<br>        print("---------------------------------------")<br>        print(f"Caught expected RuntimeError: {e}")<br>        print("---------------------------------------")<br>        print("\nThis traceback confirms that the minimal script has triggered the MIOpen bug.")<br>        print("You can now use this self-contained script in your GitHub issue report.")</pre>
</details>
